sentences.text: 3. It has been argued by learned counsel for the appellants that the impugned order is against facts and law and thus, liable to be set aside.
The first information report of this case has been lodged by respondent No.2 making false and baseless allegations.
Only general allegations have been levelled against all the accused persons and that no specific role has been assigned to any of the accused appellants.
The informant has not sustained any injury.

Learned counsel submitted that even as per prosecution version, the alleged incident took place inside the house of the complainant and thus, it cannot be said that the complainant was abused or humiliated in public view and thus, no offence under the provisions of SC/ST Act is made out.
In this connection, learned counsel has placed reliance upon the case of Gorige Pentaiah vs. State of A.P. and others [(2009)2ALT(Cri)2749].

entities.text: Gorige Pentaiah vs. State of A.P. and others [(2009)2ALT(Cri)2749]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Referring to the facts of the matter, it was submitted that prima facie no case is made out against the appellants and thus, impugned order is liable to be set aside.

4. Learned AGA and learned counsel for respondent No.2 have opposed the appeal and argued that there are allegations against the appellants that they have abused the informant and his wife by using caste indicative words and assaulted them and thus, in view of the material on record a case under the provisions of SC/ST Act is made out.
Similarly, a prima facie case for aforesaid offences under section IPC is also made out.
5. I have considered rival submissions and perused record.

6. It is well settled that at the stage of cognizance and at the stage of issuing process to the accused,
the Magistrate / Court has to be satisfied that there is sufficient ground for proceeding.
The court has to consider whether there is sufficient ground for proceeding and not whether there is sufficient ground for conviction.

At the stage of issuing the process to the accused, the Magistrate is not required to record reasons, particularly when the cognizance is being taken on the basis of report filed by the police after investigation, under section 173(2) Cr.P.C.

In S.K. Sinha, Chief Enforcement Officer v. Videocon International Limited and Ors. MANU/SC/7011/2008 : (2008) 2 SCC 492, it was held that taking cognizance has no esoteric or mystic significance in criminal law and it connotes that a judicial notice is taken of an offence, after application of mind.

entities.text: S.K. Sinha, Chief Enforcement Officer v. Videocon International Limited and Ors. MANU/SC/7011/2008 : (2008) 2 SCC 492
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Taking of cognizance is thus a condition precedent for holding a valid trial.

In M/s. India Carat Pvt. Ltd. Vs. State of Karnataka MANU/SC/0349/1989: 1989(26) ACC 280 (SC), the Supreme Court has observed that Magistrate can take into account statements of witnesses examined by Police during investigation,
take cognizance of offence complained of, order to issue a process to accused.
7.

entities.text: M/s. India Carat Pvt. Ltd. Vs. State of Karnataka MANU/SC/0349/1989: 1989(26) ACC 280 (SC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In Mehmood Ul Rehman v. Khazir Mohammad Tunda and others (2015) 12 SCC 420, it was held as under:-
"21.

entities.text: Mehmood Ul Rehman v. Khazir Mohammad Tunda and others (2015) 12 SCC 420
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Under Section 190(1)(b) Cr.P.C, the Magistrate has the advantage of a police report and under Section 190(1)(c) Cr.P.C., he has the information or knowledge of commission of an offence.
But The order of the Magistrate summoning the accused must reflect that he has applied his mind to the facts of the case and the law applicable thereto.

The application of mind has to be indicated by disclosure of mind Surendra Kumar @ Pappu Singh And 3 Others vs State Of U.P. Through Principal ... on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72906056/
2 on the satisfaction.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Considering the duties on the part of the Magistrate for issuance of summons to accused in a complaint case and that there must be sufficient indication as to the application of mind and observing that the Magistrate is not to act as a post office in taking cognizance of the complaint, under Section 190(1)(a)
Cr.P.C., he has only a complaint before him.
The Code hence specifies that "a complaint of facts which constitute such offence".
Therefore, if the complaint, on the face of it, does not disclose the commission of any offence, the Magistrate shall not take cognizance under Section 190(1)(a) Cr.P.C.
The complaint is simply to be rejected."

8. Thus, in so far as taking cognizance based on the police report is concerned, the Magistrate/ court has the advantage of the charge sheet, statement of witnesses and other evidence collected by the police during the investigation.
For issuance of process against the accused, only it has to be seen whether there is sufficient ground for proceeding against the accused.
At the stage of issuance of process, the Court is not required to weigh the evidentiary value of the materials on record.
The Court must apply its mind to the allegations in the charge sheet and the evidence produced and satisfy itself that there is sufficient ground to proceed against the accused.
The Court is not to examine the merits and demerits of the case and not to determine the adequacy of the evidence for holding the accused guilty.
The Court is also not required to embark upon the possible defenses.
Likewise, 'possible defences' need not be taken into consideration at the time of issuing process unless there is an ex- facie defence such as a legal bar or if in law the accused is not liable.

In this connection a reference may also be made to Nupur Talwar v. Central Bureau of Investigation and another (2012)11 SCC465.
9.

entities.text: Nupur Talwar v. Central Bureau of Investigation and another (2012)11 SCC465
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the instant case, perusal of record shows that the informant has lodged first information report against appellants, alleging that on 18.08.2021 at about 08.00 AM, all the accused-appellants started digging courtyard of the house of informant and when the informant objected, they abused him by using caste indicative words ''dhobia' and assaulted him and his wife by entering into his house.

In view of statement of the informant under section 161 CrPC, it appears that alleged incident of abusing took place outside the house of informant and thereafter incident of assault took place inside the house of the informant.
Though as per statement of wife of informant, the alleged incident took place inside the house but at this stage matter can not be examined meticulously.

In case of Gorige Pentalah (supra) the case was under section 3(1)(x) of SC/ST Act and section 447/427/506 IPC and it was observed by the Hon'ble Apex Court that as the incident did not take place in public view and the complainant has not alleged that accused was not a member scheduled caste or scheduled tribe and that the ingredients of section 506 IPC were not made out, thus, the proceedings were quashed.
In the instant case in the first information report itself it was mentioned that the informant is member of scheduled caste whereas the accused-appellants belong to general caste ''Chhatirya thakur'.
As per the first information report and statement of informant the alleged incident of abusing took place outside his house and thereafter incident took place inside the house of informant.
Thus, the appellants do not get any benefit from the said case law.
In view of these facts and circumstances, no case for quashing of impugned summoning order is made out.
As stated above at the stage of cognizance and summoning on the basis of charge sheet, only a prima facie case is to be seen.
At this stage matter can not be examined meticulously.

Considering entire facts,

sentences.text: no case for quashing of impugned cognizance/ summoning is made out and thus, the appeal is liable to be dismissed.

10. However, considering facts of the matter it is directed that in case appellants appear/ surrender before the Court below within a period of three weeks from today and apply for bail, their bail application shall be considered and decided expeditiously in accordance with settled law.
11. With aforesaid observations the appeal is dismissed.
